chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Salim ibn Abi Salama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about the dogs, so he said: 'Every entirely black one is a beast, and every entirely red one is a beast, and every entirely white one is a beast; that is a creation from the dogs from the Jinn, and whatever is speckled is a morphed form from the Jinn and humans.'

key_terms.بَهِيمٌ: beast/animal (specifically referring to a distinct creature type)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between black dogs and speckled dogs in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes dogs by color, identifying solid-colored varieties (black, red, white) as a distinct creation of the Jinn, while speckled (ablq) dogs are described as a hybrid morph of Jinn and humans. This classification reflects the Shia tradition of linking physical traits to metaphysical origins, offering a cosmological perspective on animal taxonomy that complements legal rulings on their purity. The distinction underscores the belief in the spiritual agency of animals, particularly dogs, within the unseen world.
